title: Rollback confirmation modal copy (blast radius + type-to-confirm)
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Safe apply + rollback mechanism (Cost Optimization Automation)
description: Design + product copy for the Rollback confirmation modal in Console. Covers: blast radius summary, type-to-confirm pattern, irreversible warning copy (where applicable), and error/edge-case strings (partial rollout, missing permissions, stale version, etc.).
body:
## Context
Operators/customer admins can revert an Optimization Config to a prior known-good version. Rollback is safety-critical and must prevent accidental broad changes, clearly communicate blast radius, and set expectations about propagation + transient effects.

This ticket focuses on **confirmation UX copy** (not layout). Layout is handled in DES-211; diff view in DES-212.

## Principles
1) Make blast radius explicit and scannable (who/what/where).
2) Require deliberate intent (type-to-confirm) when blast radius is large or rollback has operational consequences.
3) Be precise about what rollback does: change the *active* Optimization Config version for a scope and trigger runtime reconciliation; it may take time to fully propagate.
4) Avoid fear-based language, but clearly call out risks (latency/throughput impact, cache invalidation, pausing an in-progress rollout).
5) Surface audit/RBAC expectations: action is logged; permission is required.

## Modal structure (copy slots)
- Title
- One-line summary
- "Blast radius" summary (scope chips + counts)
- "What will happen" bullets
- Confirmation input (optional): type-to-confirm
- CTA buttons
- Footnotes/help text (links to runbook/docs)
- Error states + inline validation

## Recommended type-to-confirm rules
- Default: **type-to-confirm required** when rollback scope includes more than one region OR more than one tenant OR global/shared scope.
- Optional toggle (future): org policy to always require type-to-confirm.
- Always require type-to-confirm when rollback will **pause/cancel an in-progress rollout**.

### Type-to-confirm string
- Prefer stable string: `ROLLBACK`.
- Also display target version + scope so the user can sanity-check.

Rationale: typing a version ID is error-prone (users copy/paste the wrong value). Typing `ROLLBACK` is a deliberate intent check while keeping the action anchored to the displayed target.

## Canonical copy (happy path)

### A) Standard rollback (tenant/model/region scoped)
**Title:** Confirm rollback

**Summary line:** Revert optimization settings to a previous version.

**Blast radius header:** Blast radius

**Blast radius body (template):**
- Tenant: {tenant_name}
- Model: {model_name}
- Region(s): {region_list}
- Workers affected (est.): {worker_count_estimate}

If worker estimate is not available, omit that row.

**What will happen header:** What will happen

**Bullets:**
- We will set the active Optimization Config to **{target_version}** for this scope.
- The runtime will reconcile workers and apply changes gradually. Full propagation typically takes **up to {eta_minutes} minutes**.
- You can re-apply a different version at any time.

**Risk note (conditionally shown):**
- If this rollback changes caching behavior, you may see a **temporary latency increase** while caches warm.

**Confirmation input label (if required):** Type ROLLBACK to confirm

**Primary CTA:** Roll back to {target_version}

**Secondary CTA:** Cancel

**Footer:** This action will be recorded in audit logs.


### B) Broad rollback (multi-region / org-wide)
**Title:** Confirm rollback (high blast radius)

**Summary line:** This will affect production traffic across multiple regions.

**Blast radius header:** Blast radius

**Blast radius body (template):**
- Tenants affected: {tenant_count} (or “All tenants”)
- Models affected: {model_count} (or list if <= 3)
- Regions affected: {region_count} (or list if <= 3)

**Warning callout title:** Review before you proceed

**Warning callout body:**
Rolling back optimization settings at this scope can change latency/throughput characteristics quickly. If you’re responding to an incident, confirm you’re targeting the intended scope.

**What will happen bullets (same as A)**

**Confirmation input label:** Type ROLLBACK to confirm

**Primary CTA:** Roll back to {target_version}

**Secondary CTA:** Cancel

**Help link text:** View rollback runbook


### C) Rollback while an apply/rollout is in progress
**Title:** Roll back and stop rollout?

**Summary line:** A rollout is currently in progress for this scope.

**Inline status line:** Current rollout: applying version **{current_rollout_version}** ({rollout_progress_percent}% complete)

**Warning callout body:**
Proceeding will **pause the rollout** and revert the active config to **{target_version}**.

**What will happen bullets:**
- We will pause the current rollout.
- We will set the active Optimization Config to **{target_version}**.
- Workers already updated may change again during reconciliation. Full propagation typically takes **up to {eta_minutes} minutes**.

**Confirmation input label:** Type ROLLBACK to confirm

**Primary CTA:** Stop rollout and roll back

**Secondary CTA:** Cancel


## Edge-case copy / states

### 1) Permission denied (RBAC)
**Title:** You don’t have permission to roll back

**Body:**
Your role is missing the required permission: **optimization_config.rollback**.

**Primary CTA:** Request access
**Secondary CTA:** Close

**Helper text:** If you’re on-call and need urgent access, follow the incident access process.


### 2) Target version is not eligible (deleted/retention/invalid)
**Title:** Can’t roll back to this version

**Body:**
Version **{target_version}** is no longer available or is not valid for this scope.

**Primary CTA:** Choose another version
**Secondary CTA:** Close


### 3) Stale state (someone changed active version while modal open)
**Inline error near CTA:**
Active version changed from **{expected_active_version}** to **{new_active_version}**. Refresh to continue.

**Primary CTA:** Refresh
**Secondary CTA:** Cancel


### 4) Cooldown / rate limit (guardrail)
**Title:** Rollback temporarily blocked

**Body:**
A config change was triggered recently. To avoid thrashing, rollbacks are blocked for **{cooldown_minutes} minutes** after the last change.

**Primary CTA:** View change history
**Secondary CTA:** Close


### 5) Private deployment messaging (operator-managed)
(Shown in Console when scope is a Private deployment and action must be performed via operator tooling.)

**Title:** Rollback requires operator action

**Body:**
This deployment is operator-managed. To roll back to **{target_version}**, follow the Private rollback procedure.

**Primary CTA:** View Private rollback guide
**Secondary CTA:** Close


## Irreversible action guidance
Rollback itself is reversible (you can re-apply another version). We should avoid claiming it is “irreversible.”

Use “high blast radius” language instead of “irreversible.” Only use “can’t be undone” copy for actions that permanently delete versions or disable audit retention (not in scope for this project).

If stakeholders still want a stronger warning, use:
- “This change may take effect quickly and can impact production traffic.”
- “Proceed only if you understand the blast radius.”

## Accessibility + localization notes
- Confirmation input should have clear label + inline hint. Avoid relying on placeholder text.
- Avoid all-caps in long sentences; `ROLLBACK` is acceptable as a token.
- Keep primary CTA under ~32 characters when possible.

## Acceptance criteria
- Copy covers: standard rollback, high blast radius rollback, rollback during in-progress rollout.
- Includes templates for blast radius rows (tenant/model/region + optional worker estimate).
- Includes error/permission states above.
- Explicitly avoids “irreversible” claim for rollback.
- Includes audit log notice.

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Type-to-confirm should require typing version ID?
  - Decision: No; type `ROLLBACK` and show target version prominently.
- Q: Should we mention caches explicitly?
  - Decision: Conditional note only when caching toggles are in the diff summary (Console can pass a flag from diff risk scoring).

## Notes from reviews
- PM (Paula): requested that we surface propagation ETA; added “up to X minutes” language.
- SRE (Sean): requested explicit callout when stopping an in-progress rollout; added “pause rollout” phrasing.
- Security (Naomi/Marcus): requested audit log mention and explicit permission string in RBAC error; added both.
comments: 2025-12-13 (Paula Mendes): Please make sure we don’t say rollback is irreversible. We should emphasize high blast radius and production impact instead.
2025-12-16 (Sean Gallagher): Add language for the case where apply is mid-flight. On-call needs to understand it pauses rollout and reconciliation may flip workers twice.
2025-12-18 (Naomi Feldman): Include audit log mention in the modal, plus explicit permission name for RBAC-denied state. Enterprise customers will ask for both.
2026-01-06 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed we can conditionally render the caching warm-up warning from diff risk scoring. Please keep wording short for the modal.
2026-01-21 (Kenji Nakamura): Final copy pass complete. Handed off strings to Console team (ENG-4828) and added state templates for stale/blocked rollbacks.
